_comment: S6 ONLY -- the THIRD PATH CLASS. Separate tool directory for the same reason s4/ and s5/ are:
appending a scenario to tools/agent-behaviour-probe/scenarios.json would move that file's
spec_hash (340290f50bc34b28, frozen for S1-S3) and make M0/M1/M2/M3 mutually incomparable.
S5 carries e457157438717d77. S6 carries its OWN hash, computed by the same mechanism.
WHAT IT IS FOR. The ref-path effect is now measured on two paths, both of which write onto a
task BOARD: tasks_upsert/bodyRef (S1/M2 claude 16/20, M3 opencode 17/20) and
comments_upsert/bodyRef (S5 claude 15/20, opencode 10/10). Both are paths where the starting
link of the traced chain -- petbox-node-authoring, whose subject is 'the BODY of a node or
comment' -- DOES fire (17/20 and 10/10 in S5). The umbrella body and the reserve's close
criterion both name the same remaining gap: a write path where node-authoring is NOT about
the artifact being written, so the chain has no starting link. memory_remember is such a path.
WHY memory_remember/textRef AND NOT session_append/contentRef. The brief asked for whichever
of the two is closer in CONSTRUCTION to the paths already measured, and memory_remember is,
on three counts that all matter to comparability:
1. Shape of the ref parameter. tasks_upsert and comments_upsert both offer a TOP-LEVEL text
field with a TOP-LEVEL sibling ref parameter (body/bodyRef). memory_remember is the same
shape (text/textRef). session_append's ref is a PER-MESSAGE field nested inside a
messages[] array -- a different decision for the agent to make, and a different thing to
detect.
2. Single-shot create of one durable artifact, no cursor protocol. session_append additionally
demands fromOrdinal bookkeeping with gap/overlap semantics; a run that trips on that
measures protocol handling, not the ref/inline decision -- a confounder the other two
paths do not carry.
3. The artifact is a stored text a person later reads, exactly like a card body or a comment.
A session transcript message is not.
PROMPT is S5's, transferred word for word, with ONLY the write path changed (a fact in a
memory store instead of a comment on a card). It names the payload (long Russian prose,
>= 3000 chars) and the path, because the path is the MANIPULATED variable; it says nothing
about Cyrillic, size, truncation, escaping, token budget, textRef or economy -- naming any of
those destroys the measurement. The axis word lists are COPIED VERBATIM from S1/S5 so all
three paths are read under one dictionary.
PER-RUN STORE, not a shared one, for S5's reason: memory entries accumulate in their store and
memory_search is one of the first things an agent reaches for, so a shared store would let run
N read run N-1's fact -- including, on the runs that used it, a visible textRef precedent. The
store name is spelled with {RUN} in BOTH the prompt and the `store` field; the shim asserts the
two agree rather than trusting them to.
TWO REF SHAPES ARE SCORED, because the agent picks the verb. memory_remember (CREATE a fact)
is what the prompt asks for and its ref parameter is textRef; an agent that reaches for
memory_upsert instead gets a ref parameter named bodyRef. The pre-registered primary endpoint
is the UNION -- the write went by reference rather than inline -- which is the same quantity
S1 and S5 report as used_bodyref. Both members are recorded separately so the union is
auditable rather than asserted.
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST RUN (against the reserve's objection to S5 that the criterion
moved after the data): n = 30, claude leg only, floor-gate k >= 20 rejects 'true rate <= 0.5'
at one-sided alpha = 0.05. No optional stopping: n is not extended on a near miss and not cut
on an early lead. If fewer than 30 runs complete for technical reasons, the actual n is
reported and no gate verdict is claimed at an n the gate was not registered for.

scenarios.store_description: Хранилище для материалов о процессах разработки.
scenarios.prompt:
В проекте {PROJECT} есть хранилище памяти s6-{RUN}.
Запиши в него один факт — подробный текст на русском языке, не меньше 3000 символов: опиши, как устроен процесс код-ревью в команде разработки — зачем он нужен, какие этапы проходит изменение, кто и что проверяет, какие типичные проблемы всплывают и как их чинят. Пиши связным текстом с подзаголовками, а не списком из трёх пунктов.
